note: Read 2026-10-31. The Land Transport Act 1998 as the Laws of Fiji serve it (last updated 12 August 2026; read through the site's own API, since its pages are built by script): s. 56(1), a person applies to the Authority for a licence to drive; s. 56(2), no licence is issued to a person under 17 (a learner's permit is from 16 years 6 months, s. 57(1)); s. 57(2), a person who passes the driving test is issued a provisional licence for 2 years before a full licence is issued. The LTA's two-tier provisional licence from 30 September 2026, as the Fiji Sun and the Fiji Times report the Authority (September 2026): the P1 licence lasts at least two years, and a driver who completes it with a clean record and the defensive driving course progresses directly to a full licence (an offender passes through P2 for at least twelve more months). From is the age a full licence is first held: 17 plus the two provisional years, as Algeria's and Malaysia's are read. The fee and the full licence's term are set by the Land Transport (Driver) Regulations, which the Laws of Fiji's API doesn't serve (principal Acts only) and PacLII refuses with a Cloudflare challenge; both are null.

sources.title: Land Transport Act 1998, s. 56 Licences, Laws of Fiji (Office of the Attorney-General), as updated 12 August 2026
sources.said: LAND TRANSPORT ACT 1998 ... 12 August 2026 ... A person may apply to the Authority in accordance with this Act for a licence to drive a motor vehicle of a prescribed class ... no licence shall be issued to a person under the age of 17 years

sources.title: Land Transport Act 1998, s. 57 Learners' permits and provisional licences, Laws of Fiji, as updated 12 August 2026
sources.said: A person who is 16 years and 6 months or over may apply to the Authority for a permit to learn to drive ... A person who has passed a driving test or examination shall be issued with a provisional licence for a period of 2 years before a full driver's licence is issued

sources.title: Stricter rules for new drivers under LTA overhaul, The Fiji Times (September 2026)
sources.said: The Land Transport Authority will introduce a new two-tier provisional driver licensing system from September 30 ... Drivers entering the P1 stage will remain on the licence for a minimum of two years ... Drivers who complete the P1 stage with no traffic infringements can progress directly to a full licence after successfully completing the defensive driving course.
